;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–present)|War in Afghanistan]], [[2019 Ghazni bombing]]
**Fourteen people are killed and nearly 200 are injured in a [[Suicide attack|suicide]] [[car bomb]]ing by the [[Taliban]] in [[Ghazni]], [[Afghanistan]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2019/07/afghanistan-killed-taliban-car-bomb-attack-ghazni-190707060218685.html (Al Jazeera)]

;Arts and culture
*The [[Jodrell Bank Observatory]] in [[Cheshire]], [[United Kingdom]], the ancient ruins of [[Babylon]] in [[Babil Governorate]], [[Iraq]], among other sites are designated [[UNESCO]] [[World Heritage Site]]s. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/av/uk-england-manchester-48910576/jodrell-bank-observatory-made-unesco-world-heritage-site (BBC News)] [https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/middle-east/babylon-world-heritage-site-unesco-iraq-ancient-city-a8991086.html (''The Independent'')]

;International relations
*[[Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action]], [[Nuclear program of Iran]]
**Iran announces plans to begin enriching uranium beyond the limit set in its 2015 nuclear deal, with world powers pressing Europe to salvage the accord after the United States [[United States withdrawal from the Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action|withdrew from it]] last year. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2019/07/iran-announces-breach-nuclear-deal-uranium-enrichment-limit-190707064954690.html (Al Jazeera)]

;Politics and elections
*[[2019 Greek legislative election]]
**Citizens of [[Greece]] go to the polls to vote for the next members of the [[Hellenic Parliament]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-48897925 (BBC News)]
**Leader of the Opposition [[Kyriakos Mitsotakis]], from [[New Democracy (Greece)|New Democracy]], wins an absolute majority and is expected to be sworn in [[Prime Minister of Greece|Prime Minister]] as incumbent [[Alexis Tsipras]] falls to second place. Far-right [[Golden Dawn (Greece)|Golden Dawn]] loses all the seats they had in the Parliament. [https://www.nytimes.com/2019/07/07/world/europe/greek-elections-results.html (''The New York Times'')]
*[[Operation Car Wash]], [[Foreign relations of Venezuela]], [[Foreign relations of Brazil]]
**New leaked messages between Brazilian judge [[Sérgio Moro]] and prosecutors of Operation Car Wash show that Moro suggested they leak confidential information concerning [[Odebrecht]]'s activities in [[Venezuela]] to members of the Venezuelan opposition. Some prosecutors even entertained the possibility of provoking a civil war in Venezuela over the leaks. [https://theintercept.com/2019/07/07/lava-jato-vazamento-delacao-venezuela/ (''The Intercept Brasil'')]
*Anglican bishop [[David Vunagi]] is sworn in as [[Governor-General of Solomon Islands]]. [https://www.solomontimes.com/news/right-reverend-david-vunagi-officially-sworn-in-as-governor-general/9199 (''Solomon Times'')]
;Sports
*[[2019 FIFA Women's World Cup]]
**In the [[2019 FIFA Women's World Cup|final match]] of the 2019 Women's World Cup, the [[United States women's national soccer team|United States]] wins 2–0 over the [[Netherlands women's national football team|Netherlands]]. Golden Boot winner [[Megan Rapinoe]] scored on a penalty kick, followed by [[Rose Lavelle]]'s strike in the 69th minute. [https://www.nytimes.com/2019/07/07/sports/soccer/usa-vs-netherlands-score.html (''The New York Times'')]
*[[2019 Copa América]]
**Hosts [[Brazil national football team|Brazil]] defeat [[Peru national football team|Peru]] 3–1 in the [[2019 Copa América Final|final match]] of the Copa América at the [[Estádio do Maracanã]] in [[Rio de Janeiro]]. It is their ninth title and first since 2007. [https://www.theguardian.com/football/live/2019/jul/06/copa-america-final-brazil-peru-live (''The Guardian'')]
*[[2019 CONCACAF Gold Cup]]
**[[Mexico national football team|Mexico]] wins their eighth Gold Cup, defeating the [[United States men's national soccer team|United States]] 1–0 in the [[2019 CONCACAF Gold Cup|final match]] in [[Chicago]]. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/2019/07/07/mexico-vs-usa-gold-cup-final/ (''The Washington Post'')]
*[[FIBA Women's EuroBasket 2019]]
**[[Spain women's national basketball team|Spain]] wins its fourth title of the Eurobasket competition after defeating [[France women's national basketball team|France]] in the final match. [https://www.elmundo.es/deportes/baloncesto/2019/07/07/5d2257f6fc6c83df078b4691.html (''El Mundo'')]
